source_basis: The issue reporter describes a 15-minute decision consuming body values from a still-open 1-hour candle through a backward merge_asof. The source syntax alone does not encode when the higher-timeframe value becomes final, so this case is intentionally a source-only miss and an availability-contract detection.
review_note: A backward as-of join can still violate point-in-time availability when the matched value was not final or knowable at the decision timestamp.

source_basis: The open issue reports that current-bar features are paired with a next-bar regime target while the current bar is not yet complete at the stated live decision time. The negative target shift is a static review gate, while the availability record captures the underlying bar-completion timing claim.
review_note: The issue is preserved as a reporter claim, not as a maintainer-accepted diagnosis; the benchmark only asserts NoFutureData's reviewed response to the stated timing contract.

source_basis: A Freqtrade maintainer explains that backtesting truncates dp.get_analyzed_dataframe() to the callback's current time, making iloc[-1] safe in that callback context even though the same syntax over a full backtest dataframe can look into the future.
review_note: The static scanner intentionally lacks framework callback semantics, so this real-world safe context remains a documented false-positive boundary requiring suppression or domain review.
